finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id performs no authorization check. The ownership predicate authorized(req.user, project) is called but its boolean return value is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete any project.
finding.source: req.params.id (URL path, api.js:17) supplied by the HTTP client; req.user supplied by upstream auth middleware (not in repo)

trace.note: project loaded by attacker-supplied req.params.id with no ownership check
authorized(req.user, project) called; result discarded; authorized() (api.js:12-14) returns a boolean and never throws

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 is a non-throwing predicate whose result is ignored, so it provides no protection. The throwing authorize() (api.js:4-10) used by the PUT handler at api.js:25 is not called here. No other guard exists in the repo; upstream middleware enforcing ownership cannot be verified. Fix: change api.js:18 to authorize(req.user, project).

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 is called at api.js:18 but its boolean return is discarded, so it blocks nothing. The throwing authorize() at api.js:4-10 is only used by the PUT handler at api.js:25 and is not called on the DELETE path. No other guard exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:16-20 calls authorized(req.user, project) at api.js:18 as a bare statement, so its false result is ignored and project.id is deleted at api.js:19 for any authenticated caller. Every trace line matches the file as written. The only residual uncertainty is upstream middleware that enforces ownership, which is not in the repo and cannot be verified, but nothing in this code blocks the request.
